sections.normalized_html: The number [MATH: p] is [MATH: 180\%] greater than the number [MATH: q.] The number [MATH: q] is [MATH: 60\%] less than [MATH: 50.] What is the value of [MATH: p?]
sections.readable_text: The number [MATH: p] is [MATH: 180\%] greater than the number [MATH: q.] The number [MATH: q] is [MATH: 60\%] less than [MATH: 50.] What is the value of [MATH: p?]

sections.normalized_html:
We are told that [MATH: q] is [MATH: 60\%] less than [MATH: 50.] Therefore, [MATH: q|= 50 − 50 ⋅ 60%; = 50 − 50 ⋅ (60)/(100); = 50 − 30; = 20.]

We are also told that [MATH: p] is [MATH: 180\%] greater than [MATH: q.] This means [MATH: p|= q + q ⋅ 180%; = q + q ⋅ (180)/(100); = q + 1.8q; = (1 + 1.8)q; = 2.8q.]

Now, substituting [MATH: q = 20] into [MATH: p = 2.8q,] we get [MATH: p = 2.8(20) = 56.]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: p] is [MATH: 56.]
